Anything You Can Do, AI Can Do Better

2026-09-10

In Southern France, hundreds of meters deep inside a cave, there's a room with prehistoric sculptures. This room is unusual because, in order to access it, you have to crawl many meters along a narrow passageway, barely bigger than an average adult body. Many thousands of years ago, some artist dragged themselves through that tight corridor, down into that hidden cave. They carved sculptures that very few people would ever see. We don't know the artist's name. We don't know why they did this. But they did. In a sense, it was totally irrational. Why make something if no one will ever see it? If your work is destined to almost total invisibility, why bother?

Now, roughly 14000 years later, we're threatened by a different kind of invisibility. A swarm of robots compresses years of work into a week, generating a proof of a famous theorem. Agents build working software in a day that would take a human team a month. In this world, having humans wind their way through the long and twisting corridors of creativity might feel pointless when machines can get there so much faster. This new invisibility isn't the simple lack of witnesses, the absence of an audience. It's the invisibility of irrelevance, the absence caused by our presence not mattering. It's the state of being absent and present. Present in potential, but absent because illegible to capital.

Thinking too much about the possible impacts of artificial intelligence makes me depressed, and after a while I just shut down. What if irrelevance is inevitable? That would be a horrible loss for so many people. Can we really afford the paralysis of fearing it? Maybe AI will eventually outperform humans on most economically valuable tasks. That's not a reason to fold our hands and stop. Economic value is not the only form of value, and efficiency incentives not the only worthwhile incentives. I don't think there's any reason we need to accept the value we're assigned or the incentive structures we inherit. We can make better ones. We can look reality in the face and defy it.
